tei:bibl.tei:title: Page-break reference facsimile
tei:bibl.tei:note: tei:pb milestones and tei:biblScope page ranges give the foliation of the 1822 edition itself (2r–40v), not the sequential page numbering this scan adds at the foot of each page. The facsimile is the witness against which every page break was verified. Each tei:pb additionally carries a tei:pb/@facs deep link opening this scan at the page that milestone marks, so the foliation in @n stays citable while the digital edition remains linkable; the scan's first page is its title page, folio 2r is its third page where the text begins, and the recto/verso alternation is regular through folio 40v on its eightieth and last page.

tei:bibl.tei:title: Differences from the 1822 Heidenheim original
tei:bibl.tei:note: (1) Biblical quotations embedded in the running text of Magid were taken from the Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC), not from the printed 1822 haggadah text; the psalms that stand as sections of their own are transcribed from the 1822 print itself, for which see (9). (2) The original edition's ritual instructions, partly in German (in Hebrew characters) and partly in Hebrew, are not transcribed in the Hebrew project; English instructions appear only in the separate Feinstein translation project. (3) Heidenheim's edition notes and commentary are omitted. (4) The Ashkenazi German translation that accompanied the original Hebrew is not included. (5) Typography and layout follow modern digital conventions. Every page of the original is marked by a tei:pb milestone, placed at the exact point the page turns and verified page by page against the facsimile; folio 4v is the one page with nothing transcribed on it, carrying only Heidenheim's preface to Magid, so its milestone stands at the start of the next transcribed section. (6) Pre-seder material (bedikat chametz, biur chametz, eruv tavshilin) follows the Open Siddur compilation and may differ in scope or placement from the 1822 book. (7) Vocalization and spelling follow the Open Siddur transcription, not 1822 printing conventions, except in the psalms covered by (9). (8) The order of the concluding sections follows the 1822 print rather than the Open Siddur compilation. On folio 38r the print reads: Ki Lo Na'eh, לשנה הבאה בירושלים, the two fourth-cup blessings, then נרצה/Chasal Siddur Pesach — so the fourth-cup blessings are held back from Hallel to there, לשנה הבאה is separated from Chasal Siddur Pesach although the compilation runs them together, and Chasal Siddur Pesach follows rather than precedes the concluding piyyutim. Sefirat HaOmer stands between Adir Hu and Echad Mi Yodea (folio 39r). (9) Sections that are complete biblical units — Psalms 113 and 114 in Magid, 115, 116, 117, 118 and 136 in Hallel, and 126 in Barech — are separate documents carrying chapter and verse milestones with canonical biblical URNs, so they can be aligned with other witnesses. All but Psalm 126 are transcribed from the 1822 print, collated page by page against the facsimile. The print sets them with vowels alone: it carries no cantillation and no meteg, it writes the Divine Name as the double yod (tagged j:divineName), and it writes Halleluyah as one word. Paseq is set only where the print sets one — it is absent at 113:9, 115:7, 115:18, 116:1 and 118:15, in each case where the phrase falls at a line turn. The print further differs from the Leningrad Codex in a maqaf at 113:4, 115:1, 115:5, 115:6, 115:7, 116:7, 116:16, 118:3, 118:4, 118:17, 118:19 and 136:23, and reads le-olam plene at 136:3. Heidenheim's marginal catchwords, which cue the repetition of Psalm 118:21-29 (of which only verse 25 is written out twice in full), are performance directions rather than variant wording and are not transcribed, nor is the two-column setting of the refrains of Psalms 118 and 136. (10) Psalm 126 is not in the 1822 print, which opens Birkat HaMazon directly with the zimmun on folio 27v. It is an editorial addition carried over from the Open Siddur compilation, and alone among the psalms here keeps that compilation's pointing and its Westminster Leningrad Codex citation.

tei:div.tei:p:
הוֹדוּ לַיְיָ כִּי־טוֹב כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ׃ יֹאמַר־נָא יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ׃ יֹאמְרוּ נָא בֵית אַהֲרֹן כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ׃ יֹאמְרוּ נָא יִרְאֵי יְיָ כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ׃ מִן־הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָּהּ עָנָנִי בַמֶּרְחָב יָהּ׃ יְיָ לִי לֹא אִירָא מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂה לִי אָדָם׃ יְיָ לִי בְּעֹזְרָי וַאֲנִי
אֶרְאֶה בְשֹׂנְאָי׃ טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּיְיָ מִבְּטֹחַ בָּאָדָם׃ טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּיְיָ מִבְּטֹחַ בִּנְדִיבִים׃ כָּל־גּוֹיִם סְבָבוּנִי בְּשֵׁם יְיָ כִּי אֲמִילַם׃ סַבּוּנִי גַם־סְבָבוּנִי בְּשֵׁם יְיָ כִּי אֲמִילַם׃ סַבּוּנִי כִדְבוֹרִים דֹּעֲכוּ כְּאֵשׁ קוֹצִים בְּשֵׁם יְיָ כִּי אֲמִילַם׃ דַּחֹה דְחִיתַנִי לִנְפֹּל וַיְיָ עֲזָרָנִי׃ עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי־לִי לִישׁוּעָה׃ קוֹל רִנָּה וִישׁוּעָה בְּאָהֳלֵי צַדִּיקִים יְמִין יְיָ עֹשָׂה חָיִל׃ יְמִין יְיָ רוֹמֵמָה יְמִין יְיָ עֹשָׂה חָיִל׃ לֹא־אָמוּת כִּי־אֶחְיֶה וַאֲסַפֵּר מַעֲשֵׂי יָהּ׃ יַסֹּר יִסְּרַנִּי יָּהּ וְלַמָּוֶת לֹא נְתָנָנִי׃ פִּתְחוּ־לִי שַׁעֲרֵי־צֶדֶק אָבֹא בָם אוֹדֶה יָהּ׃ זֶה־הַשַּׁעַר לַיְיָ צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ׃ אוֹדְךָ כִּי עֲנִיתָנִי וַתְּהִי־לִי לִישׁוּעָה׃
אֶבֶן מָאֲסוּ הַבּוֹנִים הָיְתָה לְרֹאשׁ פִּנָּה׃ מֵאֵת יְיָ הָיְתָה זֹּאת הִיא נִפְלָאת בְּעֵינֵינוּ׃ זֶה־הַיּוֹם עָשָׂה יְיָ נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בוֹ׃ אָנָּא יְיָ הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא אָנָּא יְיָ הַצְלִיחָה נָּא׃ בָּרוּךְ הַבָּא בְּשֵׁם יְיָ בֵּרַכְנוּכֶם מִבֵּית יְיָ׃ אֵל ׀ יְיָ וַיָּאֶר לָנוּ אִסְרוּ־חַג בַּעֲבֹתִים עַד־קַרְנוֹת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃ אֵלִי אַתָּה וְאוֹדֶךָּ אֱלֹהַי אֲרוֹמְמֶךָּ׃ הוֹדוּ לַיְיָ כִּי־טוֹב כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ׃
